problem: Existing binaural audio datasets are static, pre-rendered and not tailored to spatial navigation. Simulators such as SoundSpaces 2.0 are built for RL and physics, have hard-to-resolve deprecated dependencies, and their continuous mode produces audible clicking artifacts and mixes past and present audio.
motivation: Audio-based world models need large-scale, realistic, action-conditioned binaural audio, but the data is scarce. Clean, continuous audio paired with the agent's actions is needed to learn action-consequence acoustic dynamics.
key_idea: Extend SoundSpaces 2.0 into a standalone continuous-rollout dataset generator that automates random agent navigation, records actions, fixes the IR zero-padding and time-index bugs in crossfade synthesis, and exports per-action spectral features.
insight: The clicking artifact comes from unequal impulse-response lengths across poses: without zero-padding, the crossfaded convolutions are temporally misaligned and the audio snaps at the end of the crossfade. Padding the IRs removes it, and the paper shows this only qualitatively through before/after Mel spectrograms (Fig. 3). There is no quantitative evaluation.
method: Decoupled continuous simulator: isolates the SoundSpaces 2.0 audio backend, removing the dependency on deprecated Habitat-Sim/Habitat-Lab, and rolls out navigation over the NavMesh.

Automated navigation rollout: samples random start and target points on the same floor, follows the Habitat-Sim shortest path, with a depth-limited backtracking algorithm for pathing issues; manual action sequences are also supported. Each forward step is 0.2 m, which is a 0.2 s time-step.
Crossfade fix: convolves both the IR at t and the IR at t+1 with the source segment at t+1 (the original used the segment at t), then crossfades.
IR zero-padding: equalizes IR lengths so the crossfaded segments align, which eliminates the clicks.

Audio feature pipeline: exports the full Mel spectrogram (window 2048, 128 bands, hop 147, giving 128x60 per action), the max-power reference, and the raw complex STFT (window 1024, 512 bands, giving 512x60 per action) that preserves phase/ITD.

Batch generation: parallel workers with seed control, about 1500 trajectories (~6 h of audio) in under 5 h on 30 workers with a 36-core CPU; outputs waveform, action log, top-down map and optional video.

setting.backbone: none (simulation and dataset-generation tool built on SoundSpaces 2.0 and Habitat-Sim; no learned model)
setting.training_data: none (no model trained; the tool generates datasets from Matterport3D and Replica scenes)
setting.observation: binaural audio (44.1 kHz waveform, Mel spectrogram and complex STFT per action)
setting.action_space: discrete kinematic steps: forward 0.2 m (0.2 s) plus rotations along the NavMesh shortest path
setting.privileged: NavMesh and scene geometry for shortest-path routing (a data generation tool, not a test-time agent)

numbers_note: No benchmark results; only qualitative figures and throughput statistics (~1500 trajectories, ~6 h audio in <5 h; ~1% navigation drift, ~5% failed runs).
results: AudioWorldSim generates about 1500 trajectories (~6 h of spatial audio) from one Matterport3D scene in under 5 h using 30 workers. The zero-padding fix removes click artifacts, shown qualitatively in Mel spectrograms. About 1% of trajectories drift and about 5% of runs fail from SoundSpaces backend faults.
limitations: Material-based acoustic propagation in SoundSpaces 2.0 is unreliable and inconsistent across seeds, so it is not recommended for large-scale generation.
Matterport3D and Replica licenses prevented releasing a pre-rendered dataset; only one sample scene is downloaded automatically.
No quantitative validation of audio quality, and new scenes must still follow SoundSpaces 2.0 metadata requirements.
